question: What does transfer preserve across schemas and editor instances, and can one content-fitting owner replace feature-specific paste repair?
method: best-api-review/history-v2; first-principles hard-cut comparison; bounded core, DOM/view and Plate consumer audit
trigger: User authorized the next Best API Review ledger item after the remaining queue was listed and clipboard recommended. Audit and review recording only; independent Plate features stay separate.
requirements: Copy the exact selected and mounted authored content, including visible segment order and independent root ownership.
Preserve open structural edges and transitively referenced content roots across rewriting, limiting and destination identity remapping.
Apply schema copy policy, export policy, clipboard trust boundaries and handler/codec interpretation consistently.
Fit through one destination-schema law; preserve atomic replacement, cut safety, selection intent and undo/redo.
Keep product format interpretation and table placement with their feature owners; assess all 10 clipboard census groups without absorbing separate feature reviews.
evidenceReuse: Initial clipboard record. Rechecked current source against historical clipboard command, fragment serialization and static payload ownership decisions. Their layered ownership remains useful, but old paths and proof are not current acceptance. The related native-input review is contextual and transfers no verdict. Two read-only workers inspected Plate consumers and mounted/DOM routing; findings were reconciled by the lead. Replayed 241 existing source-first tests and a public-call diagnostic; all initially captured clipboard inputs remained unchanged before recording.
summary: Pursue cutting the projected-selection paste-only interpretation pipeline and converging handler/codec/export policy at the DOM clipboard owner, while retaining exact-view targeting and the existing compiled fitter. Complete-slice rewrites must preserve roots referenced by surviving nodes: maxLength and closed rewrites currently discard them, and the public-call probe reproduces missing-root exceptions. Table/static consumers expose the same payload ownership problem. Detailed API, atomic target replacement, adoption and scale proof remain coupled; next owner is Task design plan clipboard.
alternatives: Keep/configure: existing handler and export hooks cannot fix callers that bypass them or reconstruct incomplete slices; insufficient.
Local repair: patching each rewrite or fallback fixes individual cases but preserves duplicate transfer policy; use only as adoption steps toward the durable owner.
Change API: separate edge closure, root preservation/pruning and destination identity remapping in the existing complete-slice contract; pursue detailed design.
Add primitive: a new public clipboard plugin or transfer object has no proven independent job beyond DOM transfer, ContentSlice and exact target replacement; reject speculative machinery.
Delete ContentSlice/get-fragment distinction: reject bare-node interchange because it loses open edges and referenced roots; keep getFragment for its distinct node-array query job.
Delete projected extraction: reject collapsing authored retained fragments, visible segment order and repeated root owners to one canonical range; keep the exact-view target adapter.

Merge/move: cut projected payload decoding, handler termination and fallback policy; share DOM interpretation/export rules and apply exact target replacement atomically. Strongest candidate, still provisional pending design and measurement.
Move all feature repair into the fitter: reject blanket consolidation; keep neutral fitting below table placement and external-format policy, and centralize only complete-slice mechanics.
Replace architecture: no evidence justifies replacing the compiled fitter, frontier, provenance mapping or all clipboard layers. Preserve their independent jobs.
proofLimits: 241 existing tests pass in 10 files: 87 core slice/fitting, 98 clipboard/DOM boundary, 11 projected clipboard and 45 projected command tests. A direct source public-call diagnostic records original/preserved slice success and maxLength/closed-rewrite missing-root exceptions, with zero commits in both failures. The initial test-only preload invocation failed before probe execution and was corrected. These baseline passes do not prove newly identified combinations. Projected replacement-data, export-policy and failed-insertion paths plus root-bearing table/static consumers are source findings; no actual browser, native/device, Plate package or performance replay. No runtime target is accepted: the Task design/plan must resolve dispatch, root ownership, exact target replacement, adoption, doctrine repair and matched scale proof.
